text: The question is how a user or designer steers a generative model of driving, and what that steering reaches.
Two layers matter.
previous_sentence: The question is how a user or designer steers a generative model of driving, and what that steering reaches.

text: At the **scenario level** a model generates or simulates the trajectories of road users on a map.
At the **sensor level** a world model generates what the vehicle's cameras, lidar or occupancy sensors would see, usually conditioned on an ego action, a layout or text.

text: **Scenario-level table, 77 papers.** A keyword search of OpenAlex and arXiv (2019 onward) found 371 candidates, of which 288 had open full text; 34 were chosen from abstracts.
Citation chaining from those 34 then led to 135 further leads, of which 62 were taken in (43 with open full text).

section: 2. Two layers and one question: where does the control signal enter?
text: **Scenario level (77 papers).** Trained-in conditioning is the largest family (18), then inference-time guidance (17), language or LLM-driven methods (13), other methods such as black-box adversarial search (11), models with no steering signal kept for contrast (7), reinforcement-learning fine-tuning (5), latent-space control (3) and reward or return conditioning (3). 32 of the 77 papers are from 2026 and 18 from 2025.
